headline: Network inference and constraint models for microbial and metabolic systems
label: Microbial Association Network Inference
summary: Recent preprints and papers apply graph neural networks and uncertainty-aware constraint models to microbial and metabolic network inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of network structure from sparse or noisy data, with explicit modeling of the constraints that shape it. PGL uses phylogenetic borrowing within Bayesian shrinkage for ASV-level feature selection, and TestNet-PA models sampling zeros in microbial presence-absence networks through an EM-based quasi-likelihood. A graph neural network applied to individual microbial association networks from HMP2/iHMP metagenomes identifies a co-abundant Bacteroidales module in IBD prediction. On the metabolic side, kinGEMs combines a deep learning kcat predictor with uncertainty-aware tuning, and GEM-CM couples reaction-diffusion models to random-forest surrogates of metabolic models. What is new is attention to sampling noise, phylogenetic structure, and parameter uncertainty within the inference step itself, rather than a single shared model. The items differ in modality and maturity, so this describes a dominant thread, not a shared method.
